liner.body_md:
## What listeners single out

- **Next Time You See Me** (2 other sources): Dropouts near the start of Next Time You See Me, and another in the right channel later; Large dropout near the start of Next Time You See Me, plus another in the right channel [3][4]
- **China Cat Sunflower** (2 reviews): Reviewer calls the China Cat into Rider the definitive version; The China Cat into Rider is called nuanced, layered and beautiful, almost quintessential [10][14]
- **Till The Morning Comes** (1 review): A rare song; Deadlists reportedly shows only six performances, all from fall 1970 [14]
- **I Know You Rider** (1 review): Jerry's little intro riff to I Know You Rider makes this the reviewer's favorite China/Rider [16]
- **Good Lovin'** (1 review): The drum solo in Good Lovin' is singled out as awesome [7]
- **Sugar Magnolia** (1 review): Garcia plays a high-voltage solo in Sugar Magnolia and sounds snappy and charged up throughout [8]
- **Casey Jones** (1 review): The recording has a blip or error during Casey Jones [7]
- **Uncle John's Band** (1 review): This version appears as an extra track on the current Workingman's Dead release, credited to Winterland, Oct 4 1970 [8]

## Setlist highlights

- **Truckin'//, KSAN DJ Talk**: earliest performance in the archive; legendary: the only archived performance [19]
- **Till The Morning Comes**: rare: 6 archived performances [19]

## The recordings

- **gd70-10-04.fm.glassberg_winters.28363.sbeok.shnf** (recommended): soundboard; 13 songs; 69 min; rated 3.4/5 by 15 [1]. Said about its sound: In this half-mix, Weir's and Lesh's vocals are pushed to the front [12]
- **gd1970-10-04.145828.fm.glassberg.sirmick.flac16**: FM broadcast; 13 songs; 69 min [2]. Said about its sound: Very clean transfer without the clicks or dropouts of the shnid 28363 copy [2]
- **gd1970-10-04.sbd.cousinit.19985.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 12 songs; 62 min; rated 3.57/5 by 7 [3]. Said about its sound: Truckin' and the first notes of Till the Morning Comes are missing because an announcer talks over them [3]
- **gd70-10-04.sbd.cotsman.4942.sbeok.shnf**: soundboard; 10 songs; 62 min; rated 4.06/5 by 18 [4]. Said about its sound: Some distortion when played loud; Phil's backing vocals sit a bit high in the mix early on; Phil's bass is massive and ferocious, with a tone he may have considered over-distorted; Truckin' and the first notes of Till the Morning Comes are lost under an announcer's voice [4][7][10]

## Around the show

- Jack Casady of the Jefferson Airplane was in the house; his band played later that evening [11]
- The show took place on the day Janis Joplin died [15]
- Billing order: New Riders opened, then the Dead, then the Airplane, then Quicksilver [17]
- The crowd kept chanting for more Dead after their set, even when the MC announced the remaining bands [17]
- The show was televised on KQED, with Slick playing to the cameras [17]
- Phil's bass playing is described as sharper than at any other time the reviewer heard him [11]
- Phil's vocals were dominant in 1970; by the mid-eighties audiences had to beg him to sing [18]

## Tapers and lineage

- **gd70-10-04.fm.glassberg_winters.28363.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by Harvey Lubar, Tony Cortazzo, D.Winters; source: Soundboard [1]. Also: Quadraphonic broadcast with KSAN and KQED each airing half the show; this copy has only half the mix; The disc was retracked with CDWave; Many pops, clicks and level fluctuations were fixed by hand in Cool Edit 2000, without noise reduction [1][12]
- **gd1970-10-04.145828.fm.glassberg.sirmick.flac16**: taped by Anon; transferred by Sirmick; source: Source: KSAN-FM > Reel Master > Barry Glassberg's 1st Gen 1/4 tr Reel > PCM > CD > Wav - Received from an anonymous benefactor. [2]. Also: FM broadcast from a KQED and KSAN quadraphonic simulcast, in San Francisco; Adds about three seconds of Truckin' and extra tuning from the Knudsen Collection; patches come from shnid 145789 [2]
- **gd1970-10-04.sbd.cousinit.19985.sbeok.shnf**: transferred by R>SHN Conversion By Cousinit; source: SBD>FM>MR>R>R>DAT>WAV>SHN [3]
- **gd70-10-04.sbd.cotsman.4942.sbeok.shnf**: source: FM Soundboard [4]. Also: Reviewer recalls this show circulating as a bootleg labeled Fillmore West, August 1971; Reviewer first knew part of the show from an old purple-vinyl bootleg that gave no source; Reviewer owned an undated, venue-less 'Mother Records' vinyl bootleg of this show in 1971 [8][10][16]

## Art and photos

- Fan art by Grateful Dead: [Grateful Dead Winterland Arena](https://www.dead.net/archives/1970/photos/winterland-arena) [20]
